\title{Guardrails for the Record Race: What a CsPbI3 Cell Can Honestly Claim (23.8\% $\rightarrow$ 20.8\%)}
\author{Hussain Touhid Siddiquee\thanks{Department of EEE, Leading University, Sylhet-3112, Bangladesh. E-mail: touhidsiddiqueeraj@gmail.com, mdabdulmalekfahim@gmail.com.} \and Md.\ Abdul Malek Fahim}

\noindent{\small\textit{\textbf{Abstract:} Simulation records for CsPbI3 solar cells now exceed the certified experimental frontier (22.02\%), but the numbers rest on undisclosed assumptions. We screen an ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell in SCAPS-1D over a stated box---absorber 0.4--2.2~$\mu$m, $N_A$ $10^{15}$--$3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t$ $10^{12}$--$10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, ETL $N_D$ $10^{16}$--$10^{19}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g$ 1.65--1.75~eV with linked affinity, interfaces $10^8$--$10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$---and price every assumption with computed sweeps. At an attainable gap ($E_g=1.68$~eV) the model gives 22.70\%, falling to 22.12\% at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ ($E_g=1.70$~eV); these derated numbers, not the box best, are the honest comparators. The best point reaches 23.84\% (Voc 1.250 V, Jsc 21.19 mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.97\%) at 2.2~$\mu$m, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $R_s=0$, $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interfaces and a small ETL-side electron spike ($\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.8$~eV, adopted after a sweep showed +0.33 points). At routine settings the same model gives \textbf{20.82\%} (ITO 4.0~eV, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, 1.0~$\mu$m, $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interfaces). An interface dose--response on our own cell runs 25.11\% to 21.20\%; the published 24.17\% and 24.24\% values fall below our no-interface band and are not mapped onto our curve. Scripted parasitic sweeps give 23.43\% at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$. A Morris screen (56 runs, bootstrap 95\% CIs) gives 1.02 points/decade for interface quality [0.84, 1.22] against 0.68 for bulk defects [0.35, 0.99]---intervals that overlap, so the two are not statistically separated; repeating the dose--response at routine defects makes the interface response nearly flat, so the ranking is regime-dependent. All definition files, sweep receipts, and raw curves are archived in the public repository for independent reproduction.}}

\medskip
\noindent{\small\textbf{Keywords:} CsPbI3; perovskite solar cell; SCAPS-1D; CBTS; reproducibility; device simulation}

\section{Introduction}

All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite solar cells combine the thermal stability lacking in hybrid organic--inorganic perovskites with a bandgap near 1.7~eV that suits both single-junction and tandem top-cell applications~\cite{Dai2026,Qiu2025}. After years below 19\%, certified laboratory efficiencies have recently passed 22\%: 22.02\% certified (22.60\% laboratory) with a moisture-responsive propyltriethoxysilane crystallisation strategy~\cite{Dai2026}, 22.05\% by fluorination-assisted interfacial dipole engineering~\cite{Qiu2025}, 21.71\% with dual-interface and bulk co-passivation at an open-circuit voltage of 1.27~V~\cite{Zhang2026}, and 21.43\% certified for inverted architectures~\cite{Joule2026}. Each record was won at the interfaces and in the bulk defect chemistry, which motivates a simulation study that treats those exact levers honestly.

The one-dimensional solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D) is the workhorse for such pre-experimental screening, and the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS (copper barium thiostannate) stack of \citet{Hossain2023} is the most-prescribed CsPbI3 baseline, progressing from 17.90\% over 96 screened transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} to 19.06\% after optimisation. Subsequent simulation studies report up to 24.17\% on the same stack~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA~\cite{Oyedele2023}, while large machine-learning-coupled screens now exceed 27\% on other absorbers~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026,Bifacial2026}. Three problems accompany this inflation. First, nearly every study optimises one variable at a time (OVAT), so parameter interactions---notably absorber thickness versus defect-limited diffusion length---are invisible by construction. Second, the highest numbers are obtained with interface recombination removed (stated explicitly in~\cite{Oyedele2023}) or with defect densities far below experimental reach, and raw data are routinely withheld~\cite{Hossain2023}---we report our own data the same critical way, and where we could not reproduce others for lack of published parameters, we say so instead of inferring inflation. Third, scripted sweeps mix unit systems: SCAPS definition files store SI units while script `set' commands expect practical units, so SI-valued inputs silently inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and fabricate ghost cells (scripting conventions are documented in Appendix~A).

This work contributes (i) a five-factor grid screen (96 configurations) plus refinement (36 runs) of the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell under interface-inclusive guardrails, with a post-hoc ETL-affinity adoption ($\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.8$~eV, +0.33 points by sweep) giving a best point of \textbf{23.84\%} in the stated box; (ii) an interface dose--response computed on our own cell; (iii) scripted (not analytic) series- and shunt-resistance accounting; and (iv) a Morris sensitivity screen with bootstrap intervals, reported with explicit range-dependence. Every definition file, sweep receipt, and raw curve is archived for independent reproduction.


\section{Literature: a decade of CsPbI3 progress}

\sloppy
Black-phase CsPbI3 has been stabilised stepwise since 2016: quantum-dot-induced $\alpha$-phase retention at 10.8\%~\cite{Swarnkar2016}, co-evaporated planar cells at 17.0\%~\cite{Frolova2017}, thermodynamically stable $\gamma$-films~\cite{Zhao2018}, graded-gap 14.4\% devices~\cite{Bian2018}, and compositionally engineered 13--14\% cells~\cite{Xi2019,Becker2019}, all on TiO2 with Spiro-OMeTAD, PTAA or carbon contacts~\cite{Luo2016,Ke2018,Xiang2018}. The 2019 aziridinium result at 18.40\%~\cite{Wang2019} stood for years until the 2025--2026 interface-engineering wave (Figure~\ref{fig:timeline}): fluorinated dipoles (22.05\%~\cite{Qiu2025}), dual-interface plus bulk co-passivation with Voc 1.27~V (21.71\%~\cite{Zhang2026}), moisture-responsive crystallisation (22.60\% laboratory, 22.02\% certified~\cite{Dai2026}), and stitched grain-boundary grooves in inverted cells (21.43\% certified~\cite{Joule2026}). The certified frontier is therefore 22.02\% (Dai; laboratory best 22.60\%; Qiu's 22.05\% is uncertified), and every recent jump came from defect and interface control---the precise levers a simulation study must treat honestly.

Simulation studies trace a parallel inflation curve (Table~\ref{tab:lit}). The CBTS screening programme reached 17.90\% over 96 transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} and 19.06\% after full optimisation~\cite{Hossain2023}, the baseline we reproduce. Later claims diverge upward as realism constraints are relaxed: 23.10\% with ZnO/Spiro in one report~\cite{Ristiansyah2026}, 24.17\% on our exact stack~\cite{Nazli2025}, and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA without interface layers (stated)~\cite{Oyedele2023}. The broader SCAPS literature shows the same pattern across absorbers---MAPbI3 at 19.30\% with inorganic contacts~\cite{Son2024}, gradient-doped FAPbI3 at 20.34\%~\cite{Ritu2024}, a 28.38\% bifacial triple-cation cell~\cite{Bifacial2026}, and an explicitly idealised 40.17\% MASnI3 result that exceeds the Shockley--Queisser bound~\cite{MASnI3ML2026,SQ1961}. Section~7.0 proposes the common reporting standard these numbers would need---interface status with dose level, defect floors with cross-sections---and demonstrates it on our own cell, since the published parameter tables are too incomplete to re-place anyone else's.

\section{Simulation framework and guardrails}

Devices were simulated in SCAPS-1D v3.3.10 under AM1.5G illumination (100~mW/cm$^2$) at 300~K unless stated. The baseline reproduces \citet{Hossain2023}: ITO front contact (4.0~eV), 30~nm TiO2 electron transport layer (donor density $9\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), CsPbI3 absorber (800~nm initial, $E_g=1.694$~eV, $\chi=3.95$~eV, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$), 100~nm CBTS hole transport layer ($N_A=10^{18}$~cm$^{-3}$), and Ni back contact (5.5~eV). Crucially, neutral interface recombination blocks ($N=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$, $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$) are present at both heterojunctions, and the absorber uses the coefficients-A-and-B absorption model ($A=10^7$~m$^{-1}$eV$^{-1/2}$) so that bandgap sweeps act on the absorption edge rather than a frozen file spectrum. Our unmodified baseline yields 18.99\% (Voc 1.122~V, Jsc 19.68~mA/cm$^2$, FF 86.00\%), reproducing the published 17.9--19.06\% band and validating the harness.

Guardrails enforced throughout: bulk defect floor $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ (single-crystal grade; nothing lower), absorber doping ceiling $3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, ETL affinity adopted at $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.8$~eV after a sweep (3.8--4.2~eV) showed the surveyed 4.0~eV is not optimal, conduction-band offset held near zero by linking $\chi$ to $E_g$ ($\chi=3.95+0.5(E_g-1.694)$), and automatic rejection of runs with Voc above $E_g/q-0.28$~V ($\sim$1.37~V at 1.65~eV, a plausibility ceiling; the model sets $k_{rad}=0$) or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the computed Voc (90.1\% at 300~K for the champion) as non-physical. Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}), so this section reports computed parasitic sweeps. Sweeps ran in parallel on four workers with checkpointed receipts; of 132 grid configurations, 126 converged and enter the analysis (6 non-converged worker runs excluded and listed in the receipts: three Round-A runs, all at $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ off the champion corner, and three Round-B runs, all at 1.8~$\mu$m thickness). A duplicate champion run reproduces the coarse-grid value exactly, confirming determinism; a confirmatory run at finer IV step gives 23.8365\% (FF 89.97\%), reported as 23.84\% throughout. Absorber densities of states are capped at $N_c=1.1\times10^{19}$/$N_v=8.2\times10^{19}$~cm$^{-3}$, ten times below the Table-1 print ($10^{20}$~cm$^{-3}$, above solid density and hence unphysical).


SCAPS-1D solves the Poisson equation coupled to electron and hole continuity with drift-diffusion transport~\cite{Khattak2019,BurgelmanSCAPS}:
\begin{equation}
-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\varepsilon(x)\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}\right) = q[p-n+N_D^+-N_A^-+p_t-n_t],
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{\partial n}{\partial t}=\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_n}{\partial x}+G_n-R_n,\quad
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}=-\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_p}{\partial x}+G_p-R_p,
\end{equation}
with Shockley--Read--Hall recombination through the specified bulk and interface defect levels. Optical generation uses the Eg-sqrt (Tauc) model $\alpha=A\sqrt{h\nu-E_g}$, so bandgap sweeps move the absorption edge self-consistently. Full input parameters are listed in Tables~\ref{tab:in} and~\ref{tab:if}; transport-layer screenings that motivate the TiO2/CBTS choice are reviewed in~\cite{Hossain2022,Raoui2019}.

\section{Grid screen and adopted champion}

Round~A explored the full cross-product of absorber thickness (1.0--2.0~$\mu$m), acceptor density ($10^{15}$--$10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), bulk defect density ($10^{12}$--$10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$), ETL donor density ($9\times10^{16}$--$9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$), and bandgap (1.694/1.65~eV with linked affinity)---96 configurations in a single parallel batch, rather than sequential OVAT slices. The winner (2.0~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_{D,ETL}=9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV) reached 23.47\%. Full parameters are collected in Table~\ref{tab:champ}. Round~B refined thickness (1.8--2.2~$\mu$m), gap (1.65--1.72~eV), and doping around this point (36 configurations) and reached 23.50\% (2.2~$\mu$m, $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV, $\chi=3.928$~eV). A subsequent ETL-affinity sweep showed the surveyed 4.0~eV is not optimal: the surveyed-$\chi$ Round-B best is 23.50\% (B030 $=23.5041$), 3.9~eV gives 23.80\%, 3.8~eV gives \textbf{23.84\%} (Voc 1.250~V, Jsc 21.19~mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.97\%; Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}), adopted as the box best (+0.33 points), while 4.1 and 4.2~eV collapse to 21.92\% and 19.87\%. Two features of this point matter. First, it sits at the corner of the allowed box: $N_A$ at its ceiling, $N_t$ at its floor, $N_{D,ETL}$ at the top of its tested range, $E_g$ at its bottom, thickness at the top of the refined range. Second, the best grid point at the literature gap $E_g=1.694$~eV reaches only 22.51\%, so roughly one point comes from the gap choice alone. Every top-ten configuration carries $E_g=1.65$~eV, gaining $\sim$1.5~mA/cm$^2$ over 1.694~eV; the ETL side now presents a small +0.13~eV electron spike that raises the interface recombination activation energy (Section~5.0).

From diffusion estimates ($\mu_n=25$~cm$^2$/Vs, $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$): $L\approx80$~$\mu$m at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $\approx$8~$\mu$m at $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$, $\approx$2.5~$\mu$m at $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$. The map (Figure~\ref{fig:contour}) is therefore nearly thickness-insensitive at $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$ (near-vertical contours)---the oft-quoted ``collapse below 1.5~$\mu$m'' cannot be diffusion-limited and is withdrawn. The genuine thickness--defect interaction appears at $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, where a dedicated sweep gives 20.06\% (0.5~$\mu$m), 20.72\% (0.8~$\mu$m), 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m), 20.77\% (1.5~$\mu$m): thickness matters exactly where $L$ approaches the film, which single-variable sweeps at fixed defect levels cannot resolve. ETL donor density confirms the literature optimum ($9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$) and transport-layer thicknesses are insensitive (100/30~nm retained), both consistent with~\cite{Hossain2023}. The current--voltage curve (Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}) is square and artefact-free, with a Voc deficit of 0.40~V against $E_g/q$.

The 4.85-point stacked gain decomposes along the screening path (Table~\ref{tab:champ} parameters in sequence, illustrative ordering only): thickness 800~nm to 1.5~$\mu$m adds 0.19 points (19.18\%), acceptor doping to $10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds 0.93 points (20.11\%), bulk-defect reduction to $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds $\sim$1.6 points ($\sim$21.7\%), the joint $E_g$--$\chi$ move to 1.65~eV with ETL donor optimisation contributes $\sim$1.8 points (4.50 to the surveyed best), and the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$ adds the final 0.33 points (modulo rounding). This sequential attribution is order-dependent and illustrative, not causal. Open-circuit voltage climbs 1.122 to 1.250~V while the fill factor rises 86.0 to 90.0\%, the signature of SRH-lifetime recovery rather than band-shift artefacts.

Round~A's top ten (Table~\ref{tab:top10}) all carry $E_g=1.65$~eV; the top seven sit at $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ while rows 8--10 at $N_t=10^{13}$~cm$^{-3}$ trail by $\sim$0.4 points through Voc loss (1.233 to 1.221~V). Round~B refined thickness (1.8--2.2~$\mu$m), gap (1.65--1.72~eV) and doping (36 runs) and moved the best from 23.47\% to 23.50\% (coarse grid), i.e.\ the landscape is converged rather than climbing.

Round~B's refinement is documented in full because its plateau is itself evidence: the best ten span only 23.32--23.50\% (Table~\ref{tab:top10b}), with thickness 1.8--2.2~$\mu$m and $N_A$ (1--3)$\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ numerically indistinguishable at grid resolution once $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ and $E_g=1.65$~eV are fixed (the ten span 23.32--23.50\%, a 0.18-point range against a 0.017-point coarse/fine IV-step uncertainty, so the leading cluster cannot be separated even though the 10th entry trails observably). The $N_t=3\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ entries trail by $\sim$0.05 points, confirming the defect floor binds the optimum.

\section{Band alignment}

Figure~\ref{fig:align} constructs the equilibrium alignment from the adopted champion parameters. The absorber conduction edge ($-3.928$~eV) lies 0.13~eV \textit{below} the TiO2 edge ($-3.80$~eV), so electrons face a small spike entering the ETL. The data support reading this as recombination physics, not transport: the interface recombination activation energy $E_a=E_{c,\mathrm{abs}}-E_{v,\mathrm{HTL}}$ grows from 1.37~eV at $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.4$ to 1.77~eV at 3.8~eV, and efficiency rises monotonically through zero hole-side offset (20.22\%, 22.07\%, 23.77\%, 23.81\%)---a transport reading predicts the barrier end should be worst, and it is the best. On the hole side, the absorber valence edge ($-5.578$~eV) lies 0.08~eV \textit{below} the CBTS edge ($-5.50$~eV), a shallow hole-favourable offset on the wrong side of the ideal $-0.3$ to $-0.1$~eV window ($-3.928$ vs $-3.80$; $-5.578$ vs $-5.50$). The same activation logic applies to the ETL side ($E_a=1.58$~eV at surveyed alignment), which is why the spike buys rather than costs efficiency. The adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.8$~eV sits below the surveyed 4.0~eV and is reported as a post-hoc adoption, not a surveyed value.

\section{Device characterisation}

The quantum efficiency (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) is flat at $\sim$89--90\% from 300~nm with the absorption edge red-shifted from 731~nm (baseline, 1.694~eV) to 752~nm (champion, 1.65~eV), directly explaining the Jsc gain. The UV plateau assumes the definition file's flat 10\% front reflection with no dispersive parasitic absorption in ITO or TiO2, so it is an upper envelope in the blue rather than a prediction; with TiO2 absorbing above 3.2~eV, of order 1~mA/cm$^2$ of the reported Jsc is at stake in the UV, which is large next to the points debated here and is stated as an uncertainty, not corrected. Capacitance--voltage analysis at 1~MHz (Figure~\ref{fig:cv}) shows rising capacitance with forward bias (31 to 39~nF/cm$^2$ over 0--0.5~V). The low-bias $1/C^2$ branch is linear ($R^2=1.000$) with the normal sign for a p-type absorber; its slope gives $N_A=2.93\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, essentially the $3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ input, extrapolating to $V_{bi}=1.30$~V---a free validation of the doping from the solver's own electrostatics. The SCAPS-extracted width (0.29 to 0.22~$\mu$m) sits an order of magnitude below the 2.2~$\mu$m absorber throughout (the parallel-plate check gives 0.17~$\mu$m at 0~V, consistent in order with extra deep-level capacitance unaccounted). The illuminated band diagram at short circuit (Figure~\ref{fig:eb}) exhibits clean quasi-Fermi splitting, and generation exceeds recombination by at least two orders of magnitude at every mesh point of the full 2.33~$\mu$m short-circuit profile (minimum ratio $\sim$3$\times10^2$ at $x\approx0.2$~$\mu$m near the back contact, rising above $10^5$ at both contacts; Figure~\ref{fig:gr}). All profile statements in this section are at short circuit; nothing here constrains the maximum-power or open-circuit regime.

Temperature dependence (Figure~\ref{fig:t}, Table~\ref{tab:temp}) follows the established trend~\cite{Hossain2023}: efficiency falls from 24.44\% at 275~K to 16.70\% at 475~K, driven by Voc (1.271 to 0.955~V) and FF while Jsc stays pinned at $\sim$21.19~mA/cm$^2$, i.e.\ $-0.16$\%/K relative ($-0.039$ points/K) over 300--400~K. The 275~K fill factor (90.75\%) sits \textit{below} Green's ideal-diode value at that Voc and temperature (90.86\%), so no artefact needs invoking; likewise the adopted champion's 89.97\% is within 0.12 points of ideal (90.09\%), leaving essentially no FF headroom beyond series resistance. The 475~K end of the sweep ignores the temperature dependence of $E_g$ and black-phase stability, so it is a solver stress test, not a prediction.

\subsection{Parasitic-resistance accounting}

\sloppy
Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}). Computed scripted sweeps at the adopted base give 23.64\% at $R_s=0.5~\Omega$cm$^2$, \textbf{23.43\%} at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$, and 23.00\% at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}), agreeing with the analytic derate to 0.02 points. Shunt paths cost 0.15 points at $R_{sh}=10^4~\Omega$cm$^2$ (23.69\%); combined $R_s=1$/$R_{sh}=10^4$ was not re-run at the adopted base and is omitted. The best point therefore survives realistic parasitics, but only just: at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ the margin over the 22.02\% certified record is under one point.

\section{Interface dose--response and the limits of auditing others}

Deleting the interface blocks inflates efficiency by 1.26--1.66 points absolute at the surveyed base (23.40 to 24.87\%, 23.47 to 24.73\%, 23.50 to 25.16\%), almost entirely through a $\sim$0.11~V Voc rise as interface recombination vanishes. But the binary ON/OFF comparison understates the audit: the full dose--response at the adopted base (Table~\ref{tab:ifdose}) runs 25.11\% at $10^8$~cm$^{-2}$, 24.77\% at $10^9$~cm$^{-2}$, 23.84\% at the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ guardrail, 22.62\% at $10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$, and 21.20\% at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. The published 24.17\%~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\%~\cite{Oyedele2023} values fall \textit{below} every no-interface value we computed (24.73--25.16\% across three surveyed-base cells; 25.16\% at the adopted base). Because their stacks, gaps, thicknesses and defect parameters all differ from ours, we do not map their numbers onto our curve; the dose--response is reported strictly as an own-cell result. We could not re-run either study from its published parameters (neither paper prints a complete parameter table), and we state this as a limitation rather than a finding. One no-interface cell (1.5~$\mu$m, Voc 1.382~V) breaches our 1.37~V screening ceiling and is flagged, not trusted.

\subsection{Where the missing points go}

The inflation is almost entirely a Voc effect ($+$0.11~V) with Jsc unchanged to within 0.02~mA/cm$^2$: removing the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interface states eliminates the dominant SRH channel at the heterojunctions, unpinning the quasi-Fermi splitting. The no-interface Voc values (1.364--1.382~V) reach or slightly exceed our 1.37~V $E_g$-implied screening ceiling at the 1.5~$\mu$m cell, so those cells are flagged as unphysical rather than celebrated. Fill factor moves non-monotonically (89.8 to 87.0\% on the champion) as the recombination profile reshapes. The no-interface 87.0\% at Voc 1.364~V sits 3.7 points below Green's ideal (90.7\%): the archived JV curve stays flat to 1.16~V with no kink or S-shape, so there is no visible extraction barrier, but the knee remains SRH-rounded by the surviving bulk channel---removing interfaces unpins Voc without idealising the diode. This bounds the ``no extraction barriers'' claim to current collection, not to fill factor. Asymmetric tests show both heterojunctions matter: $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$ on the ETL side alone gives 21.35\%, on the HTL side alone 21.20\%. Raising the capture cross-section $10\times$ at fixed $N_{if}=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ gives 22.2108\%, digit-identical to the $N\times10$ run at the same base (both 22.2108; receipts in Table~\ref{tab:runs}): for the symmetric single level, rate scales exactly with the $N\sigma$ product. The same identity holds in the bulk: $\sigma\times10$ at the $N_t$ floor gives 23.2572\% (digit-identical to $N_t\times10$ at the same base, $=23.2572$; receipts in Table~\ref{tab:runs}), a 0.25-point cost against the surveyed 23.5041 anchor. (A first attempt via \texttt{set ...capture\_cross\_section} instead restructured the block: applied to one interface it gave 23.8565\% (23.8565\% on one interface, 25.1494\% on both)---essentially the no-interface value---so the set-key route neutralises rather than scales, and only the verified definition-file variant is reported; Appendix~A documents this second scripting trap and a set-then-\texttt{get} verification rule. Bulk $N_t\times\sigma$ costs 0.25 points at the $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ floor but 3.12 points at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ (20.5603\% at matched $\sigma\times1$ geometry down to 17.4433\%), while $\sigma\times0.1$ at the floor gains only 0.04 points (23.53\%)---the floor is saturated.) The computed parasitic sweep at the adopted base is tabulated below.

\section{Morris sensitivity screening}

Grid methods with uneven ranges cannot rank physical importance, so we ran a Morris sensitivity screen instead: $r=8$ trajectories, $p=4$ levels, $k=6$ factors (absorber thickness, $\log N_A$, $\log N_t$, $\log N_{D,ETL}$, $E_g$ with the $\chi$ link applied deterministically, and $\log N_{if}$ tied on both interfaces), 56 fresh simulations, all converged, spanning 15.6--23.4\% (Table~\ref{tab:morris}, Figure~\ref{fig:morris}). Per decade, interface quality leads at 1.02 points (bootstrap 95\% CI [0.84, 1.22]) ahead of bulk defect density at 0.68 (CI [0.35, 0.99])---intervals that \textbf{overlap}, so with $n=8$ the two are not statistically separated; per eV, bandgap moves 17.5 points; per $\mu$m, thickness 0.72. These per-unit numbers are not commensurable across units, and the interface figure bundles both heterojunctions and depends on the chosen 4-decade range, so the ranking is regime- and range-conditional, not a universal variance share. The decisive test is the same dose--response repeated at routine defects: at $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ and 1.0~$\mu$m, $N_{if}$ 10$^9$--$10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$ moves efficiency only from 20.84\% to 20.67\% (0.16 points over two decades), while the $N_t$ 10$^{14}$--$10^{15}$ step costs far more. At the defect floor interfaces dominate; at routine defects bulk defects do. The large $\sigma$ values and the $N_t$ dose nonlinearity (steepest above 10$^{14}$) agree. Two disclosures: $E_g$ moves together with $\chi$ by construction, and the two interfaces move together. As corroboration without new simulations, a random-forest surrogate trained on all 190 standard-base runs (OOB $R^2=0.93$) with Saltelli sampling gives total-order indices $S_T=0.52$ (interfaces), 0.33 (bulk defects), 0.24 ($E_g$)---the same ordering as Morris $\mu^*$. Trap depth is a non-factor at this defect level: moving $E_t$ to 0.3 or 0.9~eV changes efficiency by $\le0.01$ points.

Interface-led sensitivity is consistent with passivation studies in which interface-adjacent defects gate the voltage~\cite{Li2018}, and with Bayesian optimisation on CsSnI3 where the optimal thickness likewise shifts with defect density~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026}.







\section{Discussion}

Fabrication plausibility bounds the result, and the computed sweeps price each term. $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ is routinely achievable; $E_g=1.65$~eV sits below the $\sim$1.7~eV of the experimental records and contributes roughly one point (best 1.694~eV grid point: 22.51\%); $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ demands near-single-crystal quality ($\tau_{\mathrm{SRH}}\approx100$~$\mu$s). The contacts are load-bearing: Ni 5.5 to 5.0~eV costs 0.23 points, and ITO 4.0 to 4.7~eV collapses the cell to 18.60\% (Voc 1.08~V)---SCAPS's thermionic-only contact boundary, so 4.0~eV is the edge of what this model tolerates rather than a typical ITO value; the routine-defect penalty is larger still, with ITO 4.4~eV costing 0.14 points at surveyed $\chi$ (20.82 to 20.68\%) but 2.73 points at adopted $\chi$ (20.84 to 18.11\%): the front-contact tolerance window itself shifts with ETL affinity (Table~\ref{tab:real}). Both affinity sweeps move efficiency through the interface activation energy rather than transport: $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}$ 3.4 to 3.8~eV gives 20.22 to 23.81\%, and $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$ 3.8 to 4.2~eV gives 23.84 to 19.87\% (surveyed-$\chi$ Round-B anchor 23.50\%). At routine settings the model gives 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, surveyed $\chi$), 20.68\% with ITO at 4.4~eV on the same base, and 18.11\% when that ITO is combined with the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$. Against experiment: 23.84\% exceeds the 22.02\% certified record by 1.82 points and the 22.60\% laboratory value by 1.24 points; with computed $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (23.43\%) the margins are 1.41 and 0.83 points, and at the attainable gap $E_g=1.70$~eV the model gives 22.51\% ($R_s=0$, 22.70\% at $E_g=1.68$~eV) and 22.12\% ($R_s=1$). The result sits at about three-quarters of the $\sim$30--31\% Shockley--Queisser limit at 1.65~eV.


\section{Limitations and outlook}

A laboratory translation would need, simultaneously: $\sim$1.0~$\mu$m CsPbI3 films at routine defect levels for the 20.82\% case (time-resolved photoluminescence verified), interface passivation toward $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ following the fluorinated-dipole~\cite{Qiu2025} or dual-interface~\cite{Zhang2026} chemistries, a front contact near 4.0~eV, and $R_s\le1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}). Not demonstrated here: 2.2~$\mu$m device-quality CsPbI3 at $N_t\sim10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, and sputtered CBTS directly on CsPbI3 (CBTS typically requires high-temperature sulfurisation), for which we found no precedent---so this section is a requirements list, not a recipe. In-line controls, where applicable: QE edge at 752~nm (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) and the $-0.16$\%/K temperature coefficient (Table~\ref{tab:temp}).

Five boundaries delimit this work. First, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ at 2.2~$\mu$m demands near-single-crystal films, and with the modelled $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$ implies $\tau_{\mathrm{SRH}}\approx100$~$\mu$s, one to two orders beyond the best reported perovskite films; at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ a dedicated sweep peaks at 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m), 20.68\% with ITO at 4.4~eV on the surveyed base, and 18.11\% when that ITO meets the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$. Second, the contacts (Ni 5.5~eV, ITO 4.0~eV), the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.8$~eV, and the shallow off-window hole-side offset (+0.08~eV) are stated-box choices, each priced in Section~9.0. Third, phase stability of black CsPbI3 against the yellow $\delta$-phase, ion migration, $E_g(T)$, and damp-heat degradation are outside SCAPS-1D steady-state scope and must be validated experimentally, following the passivation routes of~\cite{Qiu2025,Zhang2026,Dai2026}. Fourth, the grid is a screen, not an optimiser: the best point sits at the corner of the allowed box and the leading cluster is numerically inseparable. Fifth, the single-junction ceiling ($\sim$30\% at 1.65~eV~\cite{SQ1961}) caps how far any interface-inclusive screening can go.

\section{Conclusion}

Grid screening under interface-inclusive guardrails finds a 23.84\%-efficient best point in the stated CsPbI3/CBTS box and 20.82\% at routine defect levels, with every load-bearing assumption priced by computed sweep: single-crystal-grade defects, a low gap, a work-function-tuned front contact, and post-hoc affinity adoption. The same campaign prices the routine-defect thickness optimum, shows the interface dose--response to be regime-dependent (dominant at the defect floor, nearly flat at routine defects), replaces an analytic resistance derate with scripted parasitic sweeps, and validates the doping by Mott--Schottky extraction. We recommend guardrailed reporting (interface status \textit{with} dose level and defect level, defect floors \textit{with} cross-sections, unit-system declaration, Rs basis, contact work functions, affinity choices) as a publication standard for SCAPS studies.

\section*{Appendix A: two scripting traps and a verification rule}

\emph{Unit trap.} SCAPS definition files store SI units (metres, m$^{-3}$, m$^2$/Vs) but script \texttt{set} commands expect practical units ($\mu$m, cm$^{-3}$, cm$^2$/Vs)---verified by dose--response: \texttt{set layer2.NA 1e15} reproduces the file baseline (stored $10^{21}$~m$^{-3}$) exactly, while SI-valued inputs (e.g. $10^{22}$) inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and yield degenerate ghost cells (Voc 1.47--1.53~V, FF 91--92\%, up to 27\%). Practical flags that catch them: Voc above the $E_g$-implied ceiling for the modelled gap, or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the computed Voc.

\emph{Structural trap.} \texttt{set interface<n>.IFdefect<k>.capture\_cross\_section} does not adjust $\sigma$ in place; it appears to restructure the interface defect block, and in our hands it neutralised the addressed interfaces entirely (one interface: 23.8565\%; both interfaces: 25.1494\%, essentially the no-interface value). The definition-file route (rewriting \texttt{sigma\_nleft/\dots/pright}) reproduced the $N\times10$ result to four decimals, which the set-key route could not.

\emph{Rule.} For any parameter that changes a defect population, verify the applied value with a \texttt{get} of the same field in the same script and record the returned number in the run receipt; treat a result that moves efficiency in the wrong direction as a failed application, not a physical finding.
